rules.rule: Check for wheeze/tight chest severity and causes
rules.problem: Type, trigger and check list are right (every red-box non-vital item, the anaphylaxis list and the heart-failure discriminators are present and all are consumed). Missing: a first-episode form of the complaint, e.g. (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Wheezing" "finding") (qualifier (snomed_concept "First episode" "qualifier value"))) and the same for Tight chest, which the page's second heart-failure route ('patient >= 50 years with first episode of wheeze/tight chest') and the 'If first episode ... assess for asthma and COPD' step both need. Exposure timing ('within the past few hours') is dropped, as on the gold page.

rules.rule: Check for wheeze in tight chest
Diagnose probable heart failure from wheeze/tight chest
rules.problem: The page gives two routes to 'heart failure likely': (difficulty breathing worse on lying flat AND leg swelling) OR (patient >= 50 years with first episode of wheeze/tight chest). The rule encodes only the first; the second is silently dropped, so an older patient with a first episode and no orthopnea/oedema never gets the probable diagnosis. The grammar has no patient-age comparison (only age groups), so the branch cannot be encoded exactly; it should at least be recorded as 'could not model', and an approximation considered (a probable or possible branch on the First-episode-qualified complaint, with the age left to the clinician). 'probable' for 'likely' and the and-structure of the first branch are right.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible anaphylaxis from sudden wheeze/tight chest
rules.problem: Page says 'check for anaphylaxis', so 'possible' is the right certainty; structure (sudden onset AND any of ...) matches 'If sudden wheeze/tight chest and any of'. Only the footnote's 'within the past few hours' on the exposures is dropped.

'Yes: Life threatening' justifies Emergency; all six criteria and the thresholds (<50, <33%) match the page. Silent chest follows the page's own gloss 'tight chest but no wheeze' via a recorded negative; (snomed_concept "Absent breath sounds" "finding") exists if an auscultation alternative is wanted.

All six criteria and thresholds match 'Yes: Severe'. But the level is Urgent, identical to the base 'Urgent: wheeze/tight chest' rule, so this rule never changes the outcome. Either it is intentionally documentary, or the page's 'Refer urgently' for severe was meant to escalate above the mild/moderate case (which the page treats and reassesses for 3 hours before referring); the briefing reserves 'Very urgent' for explicit escalation, so this is a judgement call to record, not a defect.
The red-box heading 'Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest' applies to the whole complaint, so Urgent on the bare complaint is justified.

summary: The heart-failure rule drops the page's second route to 'heart failure likely' (patient >= 50 years with a first episode of wheeze/tight chest); the grammar cannot compare age, but the omission is silent and the first-episode form of the complaint is not even checked for. Everything else traces to the page: all 69 claims are supported, the only imprecision being the footnote's 'within the past few hours' window on the allergen exposures, dropped as on the gold page. Minor: the Urgent 'severe' rule duplicates the base Urgent rule's level, and 'assess for asthma and COPD' after a first episode is not encoded as a possible diagnosis.
